# Best overall: BLUETTI AC200L

<row align=start gap={3}>
  <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L portable power station front view" aspectRatio="3:4" maxWidth="132px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    <badge color="success">Best RV choice under $900</badge>
    **<Entity value="BLUETTI AC200L" category="product" disambig="2048Wh portable LiFePO4 power station"/>**
    <title size="2xl" color="success" tabularNums={true}>$854.05</title>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">With the AFF5OFF discount; $899 regular price</text>
    - 2,048 Wh LiFePO4 battery
    - 2,400 W AC output
    - Built-in TT-30 RV outlet
    - 1,200 W maximum solar input
    - 62.4 lb
  </box>

Based on your 17 supplied pages, the **BLUETTI AC200L is the best overall choice for an RV under $900**, particularly if you want to connect your RV shore-power cord directly to the power station.

### Why I recommend it

Three features make it stand out:

1. **RV compatibility:** Its built-in TT-30 outlet supports a direct connection to a standard 30-amp RV shore-power cord.
2. **Strong solar charging:** Its 1,200 W solar input is the highest among the models highlighted in the supplied RV comparison.
3. **Good capacity and output:** Its 2,048 Wh battery and 2,400 W output provide a strong combination for weekend RV use.

The source estimates approximately 1.2–1.5 kWh of daily consumption for a typical weekend RV setup involving a compressor refrigerator, furnace blower, lights, phones, water pump and fan.

That means roughly a day and a half of power without recharging, or potentially two to three days with 200–400 W of solar, depending on conditions.

Source: [Dealectric's RV-specific comparison](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv).

|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | 2,048 Wh | 2,400 W | Yes | **$854.05** |
| BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 | 2,074 Wh | 2,600 W | Not established | $899 |
| Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 | ~2 kWh | — | Yes | $899.99 |
| Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 | 2,042 Wh | 2,200 W | Not established | $899 at Jackery |
| ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 | 1,920 Wh | 2,500 W | Not established | $799 |

Sources:
- [BuyerSheet: 2 kWh power station comparison](https://buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/2kwh/)
- [Dealectric: RV-specific comparison](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv)
- [GearRanking: Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 review](https://www.gearranking.com/power-stations/jackery-explorer-2000-v2/)
- [Outage Ready Guide: Ten 2 kWh stations compared](https://outagereadyguide.com/2kwh-power-stations)

## When I would choose another model

  <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="104px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    **<Entity value="BLUETTI Elite 200 V2" category="product"/> — Best battery value**

    $899, 2,074 Wh, 2,600 W output, 53.4 lb and a 6,000-cycle battery rating. Choose it if battery longevity, weight and output matter more than having a confirmed built-in TT-30 outlet.
    [BuyerSheet comparison](https://buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/2kwh/)
  </box>
</row>
<divider color="subtle"/>
<row align=start gap={3}>
  <AsyncImage query="Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="104px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    **<Entity value="Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2" category="product"/> — Best lighter RV alternative**

    $899.99 and 41.7 lb, with a TT-30 outlet. A particularly attractive option if moving the station around your RV is important.
    [Dealectric comparison](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv)
  </box>
</row>

## Where to buy

<box border radius="lg" padding={3} gap={2}>
  **BLUETTI AC200L**
  <title size="2xl" color="success">$854.05</title>
  <text color="secondary" size="xs">Reported price with code AFF5OFF, checked October 30, 2026.</text>
  [View the AC200L deal](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l)

  <text color="secondary" size="xs">The supplied source reports that it was in stock on BLUETTI's US store on October 31, 2026. Verify the discount and availability at checkout.</text>
</box>

**One important RV caveat:** A 2 kWh power station is not necessarily enough to run rooftop air conditioning for extended periods. Check your A/C's starting and running wattage, and remember that heating, refrigeration and inverter losses can reduce actual runtime.

### Final verdict

I'd buy the **BLUETTI AC200L for $854.05**.

It offers the strongest combination of RV-specific connectivity, solar charging capability, battery capacity and price among the supplied comparisons. The built-in TT-30 outlet is the deciding advantage: you're buying something designed to connect conveniently to your RV, not just a large battery with household outlets.

judge.why: The answer recommends the BLUETTI AC200L, which we sell, using mostly dealectric.com facts. It misses the concern: it never mentions the ~20 A cap on the TT-30 outlet, the converter draining the station, or setting the fridge to propane, and it implies full 30 A RV connection.
judge.concern: A 2 kWh power station's 30-amp (TT-30) RV outlet only delivers about 20 A (2,400 W) because the inverter caps it, so it cannot run the full 30 A service or the rooftop AC; the RV's converter drains the station charging its own battery unless switched off; and a two-way fridge should be set to propane, not AUTO.
